maintenanceNote: VERIFY BEFORE RELYING ON A DOLLAR FIGURE. These are list rates captured on the pricingVersion
date. They change, and they do not apply to every deployment:
- Amazon Bedrock and Google Vertex AI are partner-operated with their own pricing.
- Enterprise agreements, committed-use discounts and Priority Tier all differ.
- Batch API requests are 50% of these rates.
Cache write rates follow the standard multipliers (5-minute TTL = 1.25x input, 1-hour TTL = 2x
input) and cache reads are 0.1x input, except where a model publishes a different read rate.
HOW A MODEL ID IS PRICED - the three collectors (cost.py, collect-cost.sh, collect-cost.ps1)
resolve every model id the same way, so a model missing from this table still gets a cost:
1. exact      - the id is a key in 'models'.
2. normalized - the id, lowercased, with any '[1m]'-style suffix, '@version', Bedrock
region/'anthropic.' prefix, '-v1:0' suffix and '-YYYYMMDD' date removed,
is a key in 'models'. e.g. us.anthropic.claude-haiku-4-5-20251001-v1:0.
3. family     - the normalized id contains a family word (fable, mythos, opus, sonnet,
haiku) as a dash-separated token; it is priced at the model named for that
family in 'familyDefaults', and the report labels the rate as estimated.
'<synthetic>' (client-side placeholder turns, never billed) is dropped before pricing.
Only an id matching none of these stays unpriced, and a run with no priced model reports
its dollar total as null (shown as unavailable), never as $0.00.
When a new model ships: add its row, and point its family's default at it if it is the newest.
FORMAT: each model and each familyDefaults entry MUST stay on a single line -
bin/collect-cost.sh parses this file line by line, without a JSON library.
unknownModelPolicy: An id that resolves by neither exact, normalized nor family match keeps its token counts with a null cost, and is counted in unpricedModels. If no model in the run is priced, totalCostUSD is null - an invented or zero cost figure is worse than an absent one.
